US president says he will knock out all Iran’s power plants and bridges next week in bid to force Tehran to agree to a deal President Donald Trump has threatened to expand US strikes on Iran next week to target power plants and bridges if Tehran does not agree to a deal amid a continuing dispute over the strait of Hormuz. “Next week it gets really bad for them because next week comes the power plants. Next week comes the bridges,” Trump said in a Fox News interview on Tuesday. “We’re going to knock out all their power plants. We’re going to knock out all their bridges unless they get to the table and negotiate.”

President Trump told Fox News the U.S.'s strikes against Iran could get "really bad" next week, with attacks on Iranian bridges and power plants. "We're going to hit them very hard tonight. We're going to hit them very hard tomorrow night. We're going to hit them very hard the night after," he said. "And then next week, it gets really bad for them, because next week comes the power plants, next week comes the bridges." The president continued: "We're going to knock out all their power plants, we're going to knock out all their bridges. Unless they get to the table and negotiate."

The US president made similar comments in March, when he threatened to “obliterate” Iran’s power stations and fresh water plants if Tehran did not agree to peace terms “shortly”. Destroying civilian infrastructure such as power and water facilities would be illegal under international humanitarian law and would probably constitute a war crime. Trump’s comments came as US forces carried out strikes against Iran for a fourth day in a row and reimposed a naval blockade on the country’s ports in the strait of Hormuz. US Central Command (Centcom) said the latest strikes were aimed at “degrading Iranian capabilities used to attack commercial shipping” in the strait, the key shipping channel for Gulf oil and gas where Tehran has repeatedly carried out attacks on civilian vessels.

US president says he will knock out all Iran’s power plants and bridges next week in bid to force Tehran to agree to a deal

President Donald Trump has threatened to expand US strikes on Iran next week to target power plants and bridges if Tehran does not agree to a deal amid a continuing dispute over the strait of Hormuz.

“Next week it gets really bad for them because next week comes the power plants. Next week comes the bridges,” Trump said in a Fox News interview on Tuesday. “We’re going to knock out all their power plants. We’re going to knock out all their bridges unless they get to the table and negotiate.”

The US president made similar comments in March, when he threatened to “obliterate” Iran’s power stations and fresh water plants if Tehran did not agree to peace terms “shortly”. Destroying civilian infrastructure such as power and water facilities would be illegal under international humanitarian law and would probably constitute a war crime.

Trump’s comments came as US forces carried out strikes against Iran for a fourth day in a row and reimposed a naval blockade on the country’s ports in the strait of Hormuz.

US Central Command (Centcom) said the latest strikes were aimed at “degrading Iranian capabilities used to attack commercial shipping” in the strait, the key shipping channel for Gulf oil and gas where Tehran has repeatedly carried out attacks on civilian vessels.

Iranian state media reported explosions near the port city of Bandar Abbas, on the Gulf island of Qeshm near the strait of Hormuz, and other locations.

State news agency IRNA later said that Iranian forces launched a drone attack on a military base in Jordan that hosts American warplanes.

Trump earlier backed down from a threat that ships would have to pay a 20% fee to the US for “security” in the strait, replacing it with what he described as investment and trade deals with Gulf Arab states.

The US president said he had decided to scrap the toll “based on highly productive conversations with Middle East leadership”, and touted “massive” investments, just five hours before the toll was due to come into effect. He said the US would continue to blockade Iranian ports.

The abrupt U-turn came after three days of US strikes and Iranian retaliation on US allies in the Middle East, in the fiercest exchanges in weeks which threatened to pull the region back into all-out war. It further dimmed prospects for negotiations meant to lead to a permanent truce.

payload.title: Trump uhkaa Iranin voimaloita ja siltoja iskuilla
payload.summary: Donald Trump uhkaa laajentaa Yhdysvaltain iskut ensi viikolla Iranin voimaloihin ja siltoihin, ellei Teheran suostu neuvotteluihin. Lausunto annettiin Yhdysvaltain sotilasoperaatioiden jatkuessa Hormuzinsalmessa.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltain presidentti Donald Trump on uhannut laajentaa Iranin vastaisia iskuja maan voimaloihin ja siltoihin ensi viikolla, ellei Teheran suostu neuvotteluihin. Uhkauksella Trump pyrkii painostamaan Irania sopimukseen Hormuzinsalmea koskevan kiistan ja Yhdysvaltain jatkuvien iskujen keskellä.

Voimalat ja sillat uhkauksen kohteina

Trump sanoi Fox Newsin haastattelussa tiistaina, että Yhdysvallat iskisi Iraniin voimakkaasti samana iltana ja kahtena seuraavana yönä. Hänen mukaansa tilanne muuttuisi Iranille ensi viikolla vielä pahemmaksi, sillä silloin kohteiksi tulisivat voimalat ja sillat.

Presidentti ilmoitti Yhdysvaltain tuhoavan kaikki Iranin voimalat ja sillat, jos maa ei saavu neuvottelupöytään. Hän asetti mahdollisten iskujen välttämisen ehdoksi neuvottelut ja kuvasi uhkaa keinoksi pakottaa Teheran sopimukseen.

Trump esitti samankaltaisen uhkauksen jo maaliskuussa. Tuolloin hän sanoi, että Iranin voimalat ja makean veden tuotantolaitokset hävitettäisiin, ellei Teheran hyväksy rauhanehtoja pian. Tiistaina hän nimesi kohteiksi voimaloiden lisäksi sillat.

Siviili-infrastruktuurin, kuten sähkö- ja vesilaitosten, tuhoaminen olisi kansainvälisen humanitaarisen oikeuden vastaista ja voisi muodostaa sotarikoksen. Uhkauksen kohdistuminen tällaisiin kohteisiin korostaa sen vakavuutta.

Iskut jatkuivat neljättä päivää

Trumpin lausunto tuli tilanteessa, jossa Yhdysvaltain joukot olivat tehneet iskuja Iraniin jo neljäntenä peräkkäisenä päivänä. Yhdysvallat oli samalla asettanut uudelleen merisaarron Iranin satamille Hormuzinsalmessa.

Yhdysvaltain asevoimien keskusjohto Centcom ilmoitti viimeisimpien iskujen tavoitteeksi heikentää Iranin kykyjä, joita on käytetty kauppa-alusten kimppuun hyökkäämiseen salmessa. Trumpin uusi uhkaus annettiin näiden sotilasoperaatioiden jatkuessa.

Hormuzinsalmi on keskeinen kuljetusreitti

Hormuzinsalmi on Persianlahden öljy- ja kaasukuljetusten keskeinen merireitti. Iran on tehnyt siellä toistuvasti iskuja siviilialuksia vastaan. Centcomin mukaan Yhdysvaltain uusimpien iskujen tarkoituksena on heikentää juuri tällaisten hyökkäysten toteuttamiseen käytettyjä kykyjä.

Kiista salmen turvallisuudesta jatkuu siten samaan aikaan, kun Trump uhkaa laajentaa iskujen kohdevalikoimaa kriittiseen infrastruktuuriin. Hänen tiistainen viestinsä oli ehdollinen: voimalat ja sillat säästyisivät hänen mukaansa vain, jos Iran ryhtyy neuvotteluihin.
summary_bullets: Trump uhkaa kohdistaa ensi viikolla iskuja Iranin voimaloihin ja siltoihin.
Isku-uhka on ehdollinen sille, suostuuko Iran neuvotteluihin.
Yhdysvaltain iskut Iraniin olivat jatkuneet neljäntenä peräkkäisenä päivänä.
payload.journalist_note: Trumpin uhkauksen keskeinen sisältö vahvistuu kahdesta lähteestä. Paketissa ei ole näyttöä siitä, että iskuja voimaloihin tai siltoihin olisi vielä toteutettu.

US president says he will knock out all Iran’s power plants and bridges next week in bid to force Tehran to agree to a deal President Donald Trump has threatened to expand US strikes on Iran next week to target power plants and bridges if Tehran does not agree to a deal amid a continuing dispute over the strait of Hormuz. “Next week it gets really bad for them because next week comes the power plants. Next week comes the bridges,” Trump said in a Fox News interview on Tuesday. “We’re going to knock out all their power plants. We’re going to knock out all their bridges unless they get to the table and negotiate.”

President Trump told Fox News the U.S.'s strikes against Iran could get "really bad" next week, with attacks on Iranian bridges and power plants. "We're going to hit them very hard tonight. We're going to hit them very hard tomorrow night. We're going to hit them very hard the night after," he said. "And then next week, it gets really bad for them, because next week comes the power plants, next week comes the bridges." The president continued: "We're going to knock out all their power plants, we're going to knock out all their bridges. Unless they get to the table and negotiate."

The US president made similar comments in March, when he threatened to “obliterate” Iran’s power stations and fresh water plants if Tehran did not agree to peace terms “shortly”. Destroying civilian infrastructure such as power and water facilities would be illegal under international humanitarian law and would probably constitute a war crime. Trump’s comments came as US forces carried out strikes against Iran for a fourth day in a row and reimposed a naval blockade on the country’s ports in the strait of Hormuz. US Central Command (Centcom) said the latest strikes were aimed at “degrading Iranian capabilities used to attack commercial shipping” in the strait, the key shipping channel for Gulf oil and gas where Tehran has repeatedly carried out attacks on civilian vessels.
